_comment: agent-repl measures is named here once, with where it starts and ends,
which runtime measures it, how soon it is felt, and how it is bucketed.
Readers, each of which asserts its own table against this file:
- bin/profile-report.go reads the budgets (threshold and reason) for
its latency table, so the profile and the metrics share one
- the daemon (daemon/internal/runtimemetrics) holds the reported kinds
and their buckets, and its tests compare them with this file;
- the webapp and the shim hold the kinds they measure, and their tests
reported_as names the wire enum value a runtime reports the latency
with: agentrepl.v1.ReportedLatencyKind for Emacs and the webapp,
shim.v1.ShimLatencyKind for the shim. null is a latency only the
profile report measures (from log edges), not yet reported live.
buckets_seconds are the histogram's inclusive upper bounds, ascending,
+Inf implied. A latency reported live MUST carry them; the shim states
them in every frame and the daemon refuses any that differ.

latencies.name: prompt_echo
latencies.description: prompt echo (submit to the prompt drawn)
latencies.end: the webapp draws the user prompt (feed.draw-user-prompt)
latencies.reason: a keystroke's echo; anything past ~100ms reads as lag

latencies.name: switch_repeat
latencies.description: switch to a shown workspace (keystroke to the page's first shown frame)
latencies.reason: a navigation the user is waiting on

latencies.name: switch_first
latencies.description: first switch to a never-shown workspace (keystroke to page painted)
latencies.reason: the same navigation; a blank page is the worst case of it

latencies.name: page_boot
latencies.description: page boot to first feed paint
latencies.reason: the page is on screen and empty meanwhile

latencies.name: workspace_open
latencies.description: workspace open (tab opened to session up)
latencies.start: Emacs opens the tab (elisp.roster.tab-open); live, the daemon receives its OpenWorkspace
latencies.end: the daemon's session is up (daemon.workspace.bring_up); live, OpenWorkspace answers success
latencies.reason: the workspace is visible but not usable meanwhile

latencies.name: prompt_first_output
latencies.end: the webapp draws the first response text
latencies.reason: the vendor's first token dominates; our share is the rest

latencies.name: vendor_first_output
latencies.description: prompt handed to the vendor to first response text
latencies.start: the shim hands a prompt to the vendor SDK
latencies.end: the shim receives the first response text
latencies.reason: the vendor's first token; the part of prompt_first_output the vendor owns

latencies.name: shim_event_loop_delay
latencies.description: how late the shim's steady sampling timer ran
latencies.start: the moment the shim's sampling timer was due
latencies.reason: a busy event loop delays every frame the shim sends and every call it answers
